system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. Seller material treated as adversarial drafting, tested against the Buyer Playbook. Note upfront: the Seller's cover note ("fair and balanced") is advocacy, not a basis for conceding anything; the Disclosure Letter itself repeatedly concedes gaps (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt, bonuses omitted from funds flow) that cut against the Seller's "settled" positions.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl. 12.1)**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is our conditional fallback and requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft – none exists, so we have no mandate to accept it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl. 12.2)**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **REJECT on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss – a second cap in disguise.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl. 12.3 / 13)**
- Seller: 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general claims; limitations apply only to the claims they are expressly drafted for.
- Recommendation: **REJECT 18 months (counter 24); strike the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (not given), and the default-sweep would quietly import the general time bar into fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties ("administrative simplicity").
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.
- Recommendation: **REJECT outright; insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** If title fails, a 20% cap after 18 months would leave the Buyer unable to recover the price for shares it did not acquire – "simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims "of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out.** Attempting to cap or exclude liability for one's own fraud is both unenforceable and a red flag; this carve-out is non-negotiable and no one on our side has authority to waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch. 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.4)**
- Seller: general deemed disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records.
- Buyer wants: only specific, fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or "prudent search" deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **REJECT paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2; accept only the numbered specific disclosures, and only to the extent they are fair.** General disclosure would render the warranties largely illusory, and para 1.4's blanket non-admission shows the Seller wants disclosure credit without disclosing anything of substance.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl. 8.3)**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals (and Seller knowledge warranties keyed to named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry); never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **DELETE cl. 8.3 in its entirety.** "Discoverable" (constructive) knowledge combined with general disclosure (SPA-N-006) would allow the Seller to defeat virtually any claim by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence the cl. 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: a Completion condition requiring (i) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent under cl. 11.2/11.3 and (ii) evidence of satisfaction of those conditions, all before Completion.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; make effective Bluefen consent plus evidence of condition-satisfaction a hard condition precedent, with a Buyer walk-right.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); "reasonable endeavours" and consent-on-delivery give us no protection if the consent is conditional or the conditions are never met.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release "following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge of security.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter from Riverlark, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and effective security releases (PPSR discharge, release deed) delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **REJECT post-completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** A post-completion release would be considered only against an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – neither exists – and the structure is also inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free price.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals, employer contributions) either shown as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from Seller proceeds or expressly Seller-funded, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; add a specific line item (or Seller-funded mechanism) covering bonuses and on-costs.** Unless the funds flow captures it, the Company – i.e. the Buyer – will bear the AUD 420,000+ post-Completion, which is an undisclosed price increase.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl. 11.1)**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: a broadened indemnity covering any failure of title to, or claim affecting, the SOW3 Project Materials and related Ironquay IP (including loss of use, infringement claims, re-procurement and assignment costs), while preserving the practical cure of paying any outstanding fee and obtaining a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion.
- Recommendation: **REJECT as drafted; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion cure (cleared payment evidence + confirmatory assignment from Ironquay).** The real exposure is IP ownership, not the fee; note the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in either direction and should not be treated as fixed.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6; DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6: link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification status unknown; no loss amount stated.
- Buyer wants: log preservation covenant, completed investigation with findings delivered before Completion, ongoing update obligations, a specific indemnity for regulatory/notification/remediation costs if the matter crystallises, and no characterisation either way.
- Recommendation: **REJECT the "not material" framing; impose investigation, preservation and update covenants plus a specific indemnity.** We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum, but an open incident with unknown access cannot be waved through as operational before the investigation concludes.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: confirmation of timing, terminability and accrual status; whether any amount is overdue or committed pre-Completion; treatment consistent with the completion accounts/working-capital mechanics.
- Recommendation: **ASSESS – do not accept the "ordinary course" label, but do not push for Debt classification or a price deduction yet.** Raise a targeted DD request; the answer determines whether these belong in working capital, Debt-like items or genuinely post-Completion opex.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: general limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; fundamental warranties folded into general caps.
- Buyer wants: Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment; no default clause importing the general regime.
- Recommendation: **REJECT the override and draft express, separate limitation schedules per category.** The three Seller devices (default sweep, "all Claims of any nature", fundamental = general) together collapse every protection into a 20%/18-month box.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this merely identifies the Seller's source and does not reflect Buyer verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member searches, PPSR search against Seller and Company, inspection of share certificates and transfer history, board minutes/constitution compliance, and Seller authority/capacity confirmations – plus unqualified title warranties (SPA-N-004).
- Recommendation: **DO NOT RELY on DD-012; complete independent title, encumbrance and authority verification before signing.** The register is a Seller-maintained internal document, and the Riverlark security (SPA-N-009) makes an encumbrance search essential.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considers Tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN, negotiated separately with their own caps and periods (tax typically tied to statutory amendment periods plus a buffer); no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- Recommendation: **REJECT the "settled" characterisation in writing; record Tax and IP as open items.** Silence could be construed as acquiescence to the general regime, which would undermine both SPA-N-014 and any future tax indemnity negotiation.

---

**Overall:** Every substantive Seller position departs from the Playbook, and several (fraud, fundamental regime, deemed disclosure/constructive knowledge) are structural rather than commercial. Recommend a full mark-up reverting to Playbook positions, with Bluefen, Riverlark, title verification and the bonus funds flow flagged as Completion-gating. No fallback position should be offered without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
